ceiling_statement: The maximum feasible coordination under H1-H8 is CONFLUENT DETERMINISTIC PARALLELISM WITH ATOMIC TIER COMMIT: stages may execute concurrently exactly when they form an antichain of the declared dependency DAG with pairwise-disjoint write footprints; the committed result is bitwise equal to the unique canonical serial execution (fixed topological order with deterministic tie-break); wall-clock speedup is bounded below by max(T_work/p, T_span) over the DAG's critical path (Brent's work-span law) for p declared workers; and all inter-agent arbitration is reduced to deterministic, data-defined admission at one kernel-enforced writer seat — never to timing, races, or votes. Any stage failure aborts its entire tier with the pre-tier state restored exactly.
derivation: Three independent limits compose. (1) Consistency/replay limit: H5 (deterministic replay, pure derivations) plus H8 (third-party recompute-and-compare) require the committed output to be a function of frozen inputs alone. A parallel execution whose result can depend on interleaving of non-commuting effects is not a function of its inputs, so it is unreplayable — hence the Church-Rosser condition (concurrent steps must commute, i.e., disjoint write footprints within an antichain, with a deterministic merge order) is not an engineering choice but the outer boundary: no feasible system can admit more concurrency than the commuting fraction of its effect algebra without forfeiting H5/H8. (2) Scheduling limit: given that boundary, the work-span law T_p >= max(T_1/p, T_inf) is information-flow arithmetic on the DAG — dependent stages carry data dependencies no scheduler can bypass except by speculation, and under H6 (all-or-nothing certified transitions) speculative state may never become visible in the trusted store, so speculation can only discard work, never raise the span bound. (3) Arbitration limit: FLP shows deterministic asynchronous consensus among peers is impossible with even one fault; H4 (single seat, single-writer canonical truth) dissolves the consensus problem structurally — every agent output is an untrusted candidate (H1) and the only lawful arbitration is a deterministic decidable admission predicate evaluated at the one writer seat, enforced below the code by kernel DAC (EACCES), which is the strongest arbitration available on a single-authority operating model. H3 forces the failure semantics: a failed stage cannot be 'marked executed'; the only fail-closed option is tier abort with exact pre-tier state, which requires the tier commit to be atomic (ties to AX-11).
attainment_mechanism: A deterministic tier-commit executor, buildable now in SBCL: (a) tiers computed by the existing deterministic topological sort (systems/orchestrator-spec/pipeline-dsl.lisp + systems/orchestrator-core/dependency-graph.lisp) with lexicographic stage-name tie-break; (b) each tier's stages run as lparallel futures (existing dependency: systems/orchestrator-core/parallel-executor.lisp) but write ONLY to stage-private scratch directories — no shared context mutation; (c) the tier commits only when EVERY future returns success: outputs are merged in the fixed lexicographic order and installed via the AX-11 atomic commit; any stage error discards the whole tier's scratch and signals fail-closed (abort/skip restarts only — no value-fabricating defaults); (d) the writer-seat arbitration is the already-executionally-proven OS-DAC closure — authority-v2/capability/identities.sh pins uid 11001/11002/11003 and authority-v2/proofs/verify-capability-closure.sh proves by real setpriv write attempts (with a positive witness, BLOCKED-never-PASS) that only lawmax-authority can write the store; (e) candidate arbitration is the deterministic admission predicate of authority-v2/kernel/admission-model.sexp implemented as a pure SBCL function. Everything needed is POSIX + SBCL + lparallel, all present.
b0_gap: B0's weakest link on this axis (B0 map AX-03 row): systems/orchestrator-core/parallel-executor.lisp swallows per-stage errors — handler-case returns nil (lines 71-81) and the loop then unconditionally marks the stage executed (line 88, (setf (gethash stage-name executed) t)) — no rollback, no tier abort, and stages mutate a shared context concurrently, making intra-tier order observable (also breaking AX-14 replay). The kernel-DAC arbitration seat exists and is proven (identities.sh / verify-capability-closure.sh) but the engine executor is not connected to it; there is no atomic tier commit and no scratch-then-merge discipline. So B0 has the arbitration half of the ceiling and lacks the confluent-parallelism half.
lean_obligation: Given a finite DAG G over stages, per-stage semantics as pure functions step_s : Sigma -> Option Sigma with declared footprints fp : Stage -> Finset Loc such that stages in any antichain of G have pairwise-disjoint write footprints, define exec_serial as the fold over the canonical topological order and exec_tiered as antichain-parallel execution with lexicographic merge and all-or-nothing tiers. Prove: (T-confluence) forall valid schedules sch, exec_tiered sch sigma0 = exec_serial sigma0 whenever all stages succeed; (T-abort) if any stage of tier k fails, exec_tiered returns the exact state after tier k-1 (no partial tier effects); (T-span) the makespan of any p-worker schedule is >= max(totalWork/p, criticalPath G), and the greedy tier scheduler achieves <= totalWork/p + criticalPath G.
